title: Authorization Grant Drawn by a Sensor Delivery — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Documentation Standard
content:
**Documentation and Prior Authorization Unit — standard on authorization grants drawn by sensor deliveries**

Within the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, when the billing units of a customer's Medicare advance beneficiary notice (form CMS-R-131) for the CGM supply allowance (item A4239) are counted on the CGM Original Medicare Program, the authorization grant the next delivery of the item draws on, and so the units left and the valid-through date that delivery works within, is fixed by this standard.

### The rule

This standard replaces the grant the next delivery draws on: when the grant the latest refill drew on has no units left or its valid-through date falls before the end of the next delivery's first 30-day block, and the newest grant of the item, the one with the latest valid-through date, is another grant valid on the next delivery date, the delivery draws on that newest grant, its units left being the units it authorized less the units of refills drawn on it, no other newer grant being considered; when the latest refill's grant is spent in this way and the newest grant is not such a grant, the delivery has nothing to draw on and carries no units; otherwise the standard grant applies, the delivery drawing on the grant the latest refill drew on.

### Terms used in this standard

- **First 30-day block of the next delivery**: the 30 days that begin on the next delivery date; its last day is the 29th day after the next delivery date.
- **Spent**: the grant the latest refill drew on is spent when it has no units left (zero or fewer) or its valid-through date falls before the last day of the next delivery's first 30-day block.
- **Newest grant**: the one authorization grant of item A4239 on the program whose valid-through date is the latest of all the item's grants. Its units left are the units it authorized less the units of refills of the item drawn on it.
- **Another grant valid on the next delivery date**: the newest grant is a different grant from the one the latest refill drew on, its valid-from date is on or before the next delivery date, and its valid-through date is on or after the next delivery date.
- Only the newest grant is tested. A grant whose valid-through date is earlier than the newest grant's is never drawn in place of a spent grant, even when it is valid on the next delivery date.

### Decision table

| Grant the latest refill drew on | Newest grant is another grant valid on the next delivery date | Grant drawn | Units left and valid-through date the delivery works within |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spent (no units left, or valid-through before the last day of the first 30-day block) | Yes | The newest grant | The newest grant's units left and valid-through date |
| Spent | No | None: the delivery has nothing to draw on | No units; the delivery carries no units |
| Not spent (at least 1 unit left and valid-through on or after the last day of the first 30-day block) | Either | The standard grant: the grant the latest refill drew on | That grant's units left and valid-through date |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates and units)

Take a hypothetical next delivery date of 10 May; the last day of its first 30-day block is 8 June.

- The grant the latest refill drew on has 7 units left and is valid through 8 June: it is not spent, and the delivery draws on it.
- The same grant is valid through 7 June: it is spent. The newest grant, valid from 15 April through a date in the following year and authorizing 13 units with none yet drawn, is another grant valid on 10 May, so the delivery draws on it with 13 units left.
- The same grant has no units left, and the newest grant is valid only from 20 May: it is not valid on 10 May, so the delivery has nothing to draw on and carries no units, even if a third grant whose valid-through date is earlier than the newest grant's is valid on 10 May.
- The same grant has no units left, and the newest grant of the item is that same grant: the newest grant is not another grant, so the delivery has nothing to draw on.
- A newest grant valid through exactly 10 May is valid on the next delivery date; one whose valid-from date is 11 May is not.
